name: Canada
prevalence_note: Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre 2025-2026: fake CRA or Service Canada agents threatening arrest over a 'compromised SIN', fake CBSA parcel holds, and grandparent emergency scams with cash couriers dominate.
cross_border_note: Cross-border scam call centres spoof +1 Canadian area codes and official Government of Canada numbers (CRA/ARC, Service Canada, RCMP/GRC, and CBSA) via international VoIP trunks despite CRTC STIR/SHAKEN authentication, targeting English- and French-speaking households nationwide.

scams.name: Fake CRA / Service Canada (compromised SIN, arrest threat)
scams.name_en: Fake Canada Revenue Agency or Service Canada agent threatening arrest over a compromised SIN
scams.signals_en: Poses as CRA or Service Canada saying the owner's SIN is compromised or taxes are unpaid and the RCMP will arrest them unless they pay at once by gift cards, crypto ATM or e-Transfer.
scams.legit_en: Real CRA and Service Canada contact people mostly by mail or My Account messages and never threaten arrest or ask for gift cards, crypto or e-Transfers.
bait_tactics: Sound worried and ask them to explain slowly which tax year it is about while you look for your old tax papers
Say your SIN card is in a drawer somewhere and keep asking which office and agent number to write down

scams.name: Grandparent scam (bail money, cash courier)
scams.name_en: Grandparent emergency scam asking for bail money through a cash courier
scams.signals_en: A 'grandchild' or a 'lawyer' says the grandchild crashed a car and sits in jail, needs bail money now, asks to keep it secret from the parents and sends a courier for cash.
scams.legit_en: Real family emergencies come with names and details the family can check, and courts never send couriers to collect bail cash at the door.
bait_tactics: Act shaken and ask the 'grandchild' about family things while you look for your reading glasses
Ask slowly how the courier will find the house and what the receipt will look like

scams.name: Fake CBSA intercepted parcel
scams.name_en: Fake Canada Border Services Agency call about an intercepted parcel in the owner's name
scams.signals_en: Poses as CBSA saying a parcel in the owner's name with drugs or illegal bank cards was intercepted, then transfers to 'police' and asks for money to clear their name.
scams.legit_en: Real couriers and CBSA notices about parcels the owner expects ask only for duties through the courier, with no threats or transfers to police.
bait_tactics: Sound confused and ask them to read out every item and the sender's address slowly
Say you have to find the shipping email first and ask what the parcel looked like

scams.name: Fausse Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) / Service Canada — NAS compromis
scams.name_en: French-language fake Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) or Service Canada SIN arrest threat scam
scams.signals_en: French-language robocall or live caller impersonating l'Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), Service Canada, or the RCMP (GRC) claims the victim's Social Insurance Number (numéro d'assurance sociale / NAS) is compromised or taxes are owed...
scams.legit_en: L'Agence du revenu du Canada and Service Canada never threaten arrest or prison over the phone, never suspend a Social Insurance Number by automated call, and never demand payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or urgent Interac transfers.
bait_tactics: Dites poliment que vous cherchez vos lunettes de lecture à l'étage et demandez quelle année d'imposition figure sur l'avis de cotisation
Expliquez que la ligne grésille à cause de la météo et demandez à l'interlocuteur d'épeler lentement le nom officiel de sa direction

scams.name: Arnaque des grands-parents / Besoin urgent d'argent (caution)
scams.name_en: French-language grandparent emergency bail and courier cash scam
scams.signals_en: Caller speaks French posing as a distressed grandchild after a car accident or arrest—followed by a fake police officer, bailiff, or lawyer—claiming a court 'gag order' (ordonnance de bâillon) and demanding urgent cash handed to a courier or cryptocurrency...
scams.legit_en: The Canadian criminal justice system never releases detainees in exchange for cash handed to a courier, gift cards, or cryptocurrency, and real family emergencies can always be verified by hanging up and calling the relative's known number.
bait_tactics: Dites que la voix semble enrouée sur la ligne et demandez quel membre de la famille appelle sans jamais mentionner de prénom
Répondez que votre limite de retrait au guichet est très basse et que vous allez d'abord appeler les parents sur leur numéro habituel
